articles.description:
New!
  
We’re reaching out to inform you about an important change in how payments are processed for your Booking.com reservations through Smily. We have introduced a new multi-payment schedule to better align with Booking.com’s guidelines and ensure guests are charged accurately at the correct times.
You are impacted by this change only if you are not using payment by booking but using regular credit card payment with guests and whether you are in partial or full sync.
What’s changing
Multiple payments: In cases where your cancellation policy required 100% pre-payment (or was entirely non-refundable), our old process often took the entire amount up front (including fees and taxes). Now, for policies with partial refunds or partial pre-payments (e.g., a 50–50 split), we align fully with Bo…
articles.title: Important Update: New multi-Payment schedule for your Booking.com Reservations

articles.author: Basile, Product Manager
articles.description:
New!
  
We’re excited to announce our integration with a new Booking.com’s API, bringing you clearer insights into each reservation’s fees and taxes. 
Those new informations are available for all Property Managers using Payment by booking (with VCC and Bank transfer), whether you’re using partial or full sync with Booking.com.
What’s New?
Detailed price breakdown: You’ll now see clearer information on rental fees, cleaning fees, service charges, and city taxes directly in the reservation details as below; 



Withheld tax details: In regions where Booking.com withholds tax on your behalf, you’ll see exactly how much was withheld and paid to authorities.


Current balance & VCC info: More visibility on the Virtual Credit Card (VCC) balance, plus its activation and expiration dates.


    
How Does this affect you?
Depending on how Booking.com handles the city tax for each reservation, you’ll see one of these scenarios:
1- Booking.com collects and remits city tax directly to the authorities:
Your payment bar will show two payments (one for the rental and one for the withheld tax).

Since Booking.com pays the tax on your behalf, the payment bar will appear “complete.”
2- Booking.com collects the city tax from the guest and includes it in the VCC; you are responsible for remitting the tax:
The city tax is included in your total payout, so the payment bar will also appear “complete.”


Don’t forget to pay the tax to your local authorities.


3- Booking.com does not collect the city tax; you must collect and remit it yourself:
The payment bar will show the rental amount only (city tax is missing).


You must collect the city tax from guests at check-in and pay it to the authorities.


The city tax is missing from the payment bar, you should collect it before/on check-in.


-> Automatic payment link should be disabled in these cases, Booking.com does not include it in the payment because of regulations.
If you have any questions, please reach out to us 🙂
Your Smily team!
articles.title: Booking.com - Introducing clearer fee & tax breakdown for your reservations

articles.author: Basile, Product Manager
articles.description:
New!
  
We’ve enabled Booking.com self-service requests directly in the Smily PMS inbox! 🎉
When guests send special requests (extra bed, early check-in, etc.) during or after their booking, these requests will appear directly in your Smily inbox. 📩
Requests include: check-in/out time, date change, free cancellation, parking, bed preference, extra crib, extra bed
💡 What does this mean for you?
1️⃣ Monitor your Smily inbox to see potential guest requests from Booking.com.
These messages will appear just like regular messages.
2️⃣ Choose where to respond:
✅ If you want to continue using Booking.com’s automation, reply via the Extranet using the quick-response options like below ⬇️

✍️ If you prefer to handle the request manually, reply with free text in Smily. (⚠️ This will end the automated flow for that request.)
3️⃣ Be vigilant with cancellations and date changes 📆
These will always be sent as free text and will require manual action on your part.
🔎 Important clarifications
1️⃣ Quick-response options (as shown above) are only available on the Booking.com Extranet
Guests can submit their self-service requests (e.g., “Extra bed request,” “Check-in time change”), and you will see these new messages in Smily.

However, you cannot use the quick-response buttons (e.g., “Confirm for free,” “Confirm with charges,” etc.) from Smily.
👉 If you want to use these buttons, you must do so via the Booking.com Extranet. In Smily, you can only respond with a free-text message. ✍️
2️⃣ No automated cancellations or date changes
No booking is automatically cancelled or modified unless the guest does it themselves via Booking.com or you process it manually.
Make sure to confirm any cancellation or date change request yourself!
💬 Any questions? Need help? Our support team is here for you! 🚀💙
articles.title: New booking.com Self-Service messages in Smily

We have experienced an issue with Google Voice beginning on Monday, 2025-02-17 at 07:06 US/Pacific.
Our engineering team has applied the fix which has successfully mitigated the issue.
We apologize to all who were affected by the disruption.
### **Diagnosis:**
Impacted customers may have received an error message stating ‘The message violates our Acceptable Use Policy’.
The issue has impacted only consumer users and not Google Workspace users.
### **Workaround:**
Customers may retry to send the SMS which might have resolved the issue. Sending SMS messages from Android or iOS devices appeared to be functioning correctly.

Jan 30, 15:39 UTC
Resolved - On January 30th, 2025 from 14:22 UTC to 14:48 UTC, web requests to GitHub.com experienced failures (at peak the error rate was 44%), with the average successful request taking over 3 seconds to complete.
This outage was caused by a hardware failure in the caching layer that supports rate limiting. In addition, the impact was prolonged due to a lack of automated failover for the caching layer. A manual failover of the primary to trusted hardware was performed following recovery to ensure that the issue would not reoccur under similar circumstances.
As a result of this incident, we will be moving to a high availability cache configuration and adding resilience to cache failures at this layer to ensure requests are able to be handled should similar circumstances happen in the future.

articles.description: From 6:45 AM PST to 4:13 PM PST on February 26, 2025, a large percentage of Slack users experienced issues with various features including sending and receiving messages, using workflows, loading channels or threads, and logging into Slack. These features may have been degraded or in some cases fully unusable.  We traced this issue to a maintenance action in one of our database systems, which, combined with a latency defect in our caching system, caused an overload of heavy traffic to the database. As a result, approximately 50% of instances relying on this database became unavailable. We took several actions to reduce the heavy load on the database system and implemented a fix for the source of the load. At around 9:32 AM PST, we observed improved health metrics for some affected Slack features and at around 4:13 PM PST, our health metrics returned to normal rates, indicating the issue was resolved for all affected users.While the main impact of this issue has been resolved, we are still addressing a backlog queue of Events API requests and are sharing updates here: https://slack-status.com/2025-02/d41e4bfd1ccae26a.
articles.title: Outage: Trouble loading or using Slack

articles.description: Our work related to events is still in motion. We'll provide an update as new information becomes available. We appreciate your patience along the way.

articles.description: From 7:19 PM PST on February 23, 2025 to 3:14 PM PST on February 24, 2025, some users may have been unable to use @here, @channel or @everyone mentions in the Slack for iOS app on version 25.02.30.A routine code update introduced an error in the most recent version of the Slack for iOS app, which prevented these mentions from autocompleting or sending correctly.We released a fix in version 25.02.31 (available via the Apple App Store), which resolved these issues for all impacted users.
articles.title: Incident: Specific @-mentions like @channelname, @here and @everyone are not working on iOS app version 25.02.30

articles.description: From 2:00 PM PST on February 9, 2025, to 8:24 PM PST on February 11, 2025, some users experienced issues with custom emoji failing to load. A backend process responsible for handling custom emoji was experiencing an unexpected spike of requests, resulting in a backlog. This backlog primarily caused delays with recently added emoji. We made a change to restart emoji rendering jobs to help with request traffic, resolving the issue for all affected users.
articles.title: Incident: Custom emoji not loading

articles.description: From 9:00 AM PST on February 14, 2025 to 4:30 PM PST on February 19, 2025, iOS users with Slack set to a non-English language were unable to set a default status and may have also encountered intermittent issues setting custom statuses.We identified that a recent code change had resulted in localized emoji names being returned to our systems in error, which was causing status updates to fail.We deployed a fix in version 25.02.30, which should be available to all users via the Apple App Store shortly.
articles.title: Incident: Non-English iOS users can't set default status

articles.description: From around 5:00 PM PST on February 11, 2025 until around 1:00 PM PST on February 17, 2025, some users were unable to add existing workspace members to channels using their email addresses in bulk. Affected users reported the issue presenting as an endless loading icon or various errors appearing when entering user emails. It was also noted that some users were not displayed as existing members of the channel.We traced this issue back to a logic condition that would prevent Slack from returning proper results if there were multiple users with matching search query conditions. We removed the problematic condition within the code, resolving the issue for all affected users.
articles.title: Incident: Some users may have trouble adding multiple existing workspace members to channels by email address

articles.description: On February 13, 2025, from 11:00 AM to 1:45 PM PST, we detected an increase in backend errors relating to Workflow Builder. During this time, some users may have encountered various errors when running or editing workflows.We discovered that a recent backend change to our workflow process was creating these errors. We immediately reverted this change, which resolved the issue for all affected users. We're analyzing data from this event to understand ways to mitigate similar issues that may occur in the future.
articles.title: Incident: Trouble with adding or triggering steps in Workflow Builder

articles.description: On February 5, 2025, from 6:42 PM PST until 7:13 PM PST, some users were unable to switch workspaces by clicking the icons in their sidebarA recent code change introduced an unexpected error to the workspace switcher logic. This caused an invalid persistent user state, preventing Slack from routing the user to the correct workspace.We rolled back the change to a healthy version, resolving the issue and restoring functionality. To capture the fix, users may have needed to close and re-launch their Slack app.
articles.title: Incident: Issue with switching between workspaces in the desktop app

articles.description: Starting around 8:00 AM PST until about 8:30 AM PST on February 6, 2025, some users experienced issues with emojis rendering properly in Slack, displaying only the emoji names.We traced this back to a scaling issue with a database service responsible for rendering emoji requests. We temporarily redirected incoming traffic away from the problematic database service to address the scaling issue. Once the issue was resolved, traffic was returned to the proper databases, restoring emoji rendering functionality for all affected users.
articles.title: Incident: Some users may be having trouble with emojis.

articles.description: From 2:30 PM PST on February 6, 2025 to around 1:30 AM PST on February 7, 2025, some users experienced a "Something went wrong" error while searching in Slack when using filers. A recent code change was made which lead to the issue. As soon as this was identified, we rolled back to a previous version and worked a fix which resolved the problem for all impacted users.

articles.description: From 12:47 AM PST on January 31, 2025 to around 12:22 PM PST on February 3, 2025, some users may have experienced issues using 'Sign in with Google' or 'Sign in with Apple' to access their workspaces. We made a code change that inadvertently introduced an encoding error in these authentication requests. We identified the change that introduced the problem and rolled it back, resolving the issue for all impacted users.
articles.title: Incident: Signing in with Google and Workflows linked to Google actions may be failing for some customers

articles.description: From 3:00 PM PST on February 2, 2025 to around 5:00 PM PST on February 3, 2025, users may have experienced issues accessing some of the admin pages, as well as the Discovery page for Enterprise Grid users. A spike in errors caused an increase in traffic across part of our search infrastructure, which powers these pages. Our automatic monitoring systems alerted us to this spike, and we stepped in to redistribute incoming traffic to spread out the load. This resolved the issue for all impacted users.
articles.title: Incident: Some Org Admins may be having trouble loading the People page and other pages in the admin dashboard

articles.description: On January 29, 2025 from 7:05 PM PST to February 4, 2025 at 9:30 PM PST, some users did not receive mobile notifications for new messages in Slack Connect channels.A recent change caused a regression that impacted mobile notification preferences, but only for conversations that connected multiple teams.Once we identified the code responsible for the issue, we deployed a fix that resolved the problem for all affected users.
articles.title: Incident: Issues with mobile notifications for Slack Connect channels

articles.description: On January 28, 2025 from 5:50 AM PST to 9:31 AM PST, some users may have experienced issues loading threads, or may have seen their Threads view bolded despite having no new messages. After thorough investigation, we have established that this issue resulted from another incident. Please find more information here: https://slack-status.com/2025-01/710d9d22c424e053
articles.title: Incident: Some users may see Threads in their sidebar bolded indicating new content

articles.description: On January 27, 2025 from 3:00 AM PST to 9:45 AM PST, some users may have received error messages when attempting to add users to group DMs.While we initially investigated this as a separate issue, we have now determined that this was a direct result of another incident. Please find more information here: https://slack-status.com/2025-01/710d9d22c424e053
articles.title: Incident: Some users may be having trouble adding members to group DMs

articles.description: On January 27, 2025 from 3:37 AM PST to 10:06 AM PST, some users may have experienced issues with threads, including delayed notifications, delayed message delivery and loading issues. Users may have also had issues when attempting to add users to group DMs.A resource intensive task overloaded one of our servers, causing this task and other incoming requests to fail. Our retry systems automatically tried to process the stuck requests, further impacting performance with repeat attempts.To ease load on these systems, we limited the number of retry attempts and reduced the total number of requests being handled by the overloaded server. This restored normal performance and resolved the issue for all impacted users.
articles.title: Incident: Trouble with missing notifications & adding users to Group DMs

articles.description: On February 3, 2025 from 7:13 AM PST to 8:54 AM PST, some users may have experienced delayed notifications or issues loading threads while using Slack.A recent code change inadvertently increased load on our servers, resulting in intermittent loading errors and notification delays.We rolled back the code change, resolving the issue for all impacted users.
articles.title: Incident: Some users may be having trouble loading threads and notifications.

articles.description: Issue Summary:From 6:30 PM PST on January 28, 2025 to around 11:00 AM PST on January 30, 2025, some Slack AI customers may have experienced issues with Slack AI searches.A configuration issue with some of our Slack AI infrastructure resulted in an unexpected backlog of Slack AI tasks. This backlog meant that Slack AI responses were not served to users in a timely manner. Additionally, certain Slack AI queries had very long timeout windows, remaining in the queue indefinitely and contributing to the backlog. We scaled up our Slack AI infrastructure to increase our capacity to work through the backlog and manually ended any stuck queries. We also deployed a code change to set more reasonable timeout windows for the long-running queries, resolving the issue for all impacted users.
articles.title: Incident: Slowness searching with Slack AI
